title: Capacity Conflict in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores capacity conflict dynamics within a ring communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Multiple agents may attempt to route freight simultaneously
Lower-priority freight must wait or find alternate routes
Coordination required to avoid wasted capacity
Information propagation delay: News of capacity drop at 'west-east' must travel through the ring topology (a->b->c->d) before reaching non-adjacent agents
Communication Bottleneck: A single agent's failure to relay capacity updates prevents the entire ring from synchronizing
Route Oscillations: Agents switching between 'west-east' and 'west-south' simultaneously, creating secondary congestion
coordination_challenges: Multi-hop Information Latency: Agents must account for the fact that neighbors may have outdated route status due to the ring-constrained comms
Resource Reservation: High-priority agents must signal intent to reserve capacity via multi-hop messages before movement
Conflict Resolution: Resolving contention on the 'east-north' bottleneck (capacity 1) when communicating via the ring
suggested_agent_strategies: Proactive Gossiping: Agents should periodically broadcast local capacity observations to neighbors to mitigate ring latency
Priority-Aware Buffering: Normal-priority agents should proactively reroute to longer paths (e.g., south-north) if high-priority signals are detected in the ring
Token-Based Reservation: Implementation of a virtual 'reservation token' passed through the ring to claim capacity on contested segments
success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimization of 'dead-heading' (empty trips caused by miscommunication)
